errors.says: Every nonzero residual contains a norm-one vector built from coordinate units outside small supports, 'so it is nondegenerate and nonalternating'
errors.paper: The norm-one vector gives only nonalternation; each residual is nondegenerate by the orthogonal decompositions, a separate reason

errors.says: A nonzero residual is nonalternating because it contains a norm-one coordinate vector outside the supports of the earlier tensor vectors
errors.paper: The norm-one vector is a tensor product of chosen norm-one vectors, including the line vectors of P and Q, which are not coordinate units, so it need not be a coordinate vector

errors.says: The computed source transform is F~ = 2^gamma B_0 C~ A, with the exact linewise maps A and B_0
errors.paper: F~ applies the linewise approximations to A and to B_0 around the computed chirp transform; only its exact counterpart uses A and B_0

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and both carry the central saving chain equally. On the core items A has more of the derivation: P3 of the complex phase interface, the omitted top-position XOR and T_0's preservation of the bad set in packed addition, the exact operators with L in the transform layout, the uniform packed-call check, and the phase-product estimate in exact recovery. B's advantages are the full M1 elimination, the slot-level endpoint corrections, the layer-recurrence conditions and the frame invariant. A also carries the conjecture-negation step that B omits, and B has one more minor misstatement (the components of F~), so the balance tips slightly to A.
